 Petrol, Diesel Price Relief Not Around The Corner: Minister Suresh Gopi 
 Petrol, Diesel Price Relief Not Around The Corner: Minister Suresh Gopi
 BW Online Bureau
 Nov 16, 2026
 # Suresh Gopi 
 # Petrol Prices 
 # Diesel Prices 
 # Oil Marketing Companies 
 # West Asia Conflict 
 # India Energy Sector 
 # Ethanol Blending 
 Suresh Gopi says oil marketing companies need to recover Rs 42,000 crore in losses before any immediate fuel price reduction can be considered, as West Asia tensions disrupt petroleum supplies
 Union Minister Suresh Gopi has ruled out an immediate reduction in petrol and diesel prices, citing Rs 42,000 crore in losses incurred by oil companies and disruptions in petroleum product supplies amid the ongoing West Asia conflict. 
 Speaking to reporters at Chennai's Meenambakkam airport, Gopi said any immediate price reduction would be difficult given the financial position of oil marketing companies (OMCs), adding that their accumulated losses would first need to be addressed. 
 "We may wish for prices to come down the next day. But technically it is not possible right away. Oil companies have already incurred losses of Rs 42,000 crore. All this needs to be compensated," Gopi said. 
 He added that state governments could consider reducing taxes on petrol to provide relief to consumers, while emphasising that the financial implications for oil companies could not be overlooked. 
 The minister also acknowledged disruptions in the supply of petroleum products, saying the government was taking steps to resolve the issues and restore normal supply. 
 On fuel price movements across southern states, Gopi said prices had also increased in Keralam and Karnataka, while expressing uncertainty over the reasons behind the increase in Tamil Nadu. 
 "Prices have also increased in Keralam. I do not know how prices have increased in Tamil Nadu. They have also increased in Karnataka," he said. 
 The remarks come amid growing concerns over the impact of geopolitical tensions in West Asia on India's energy supply chain, fuel availability and pricing. 
 Separately, Karnataka Industries Minister MB Patil had earlier blamed the Centre for the challenges facing the ethanol sector, accusing the Union Government of encouraging higher production through ambitious blending targets without ensuring adequate procurement. 
 Speaking to reporters in Bengaluru on November 8, Patil questioned the Centre's approach to ethanol blending, alleging that the government had promoted targets such as E10, E20 and E30 without sufficient planning and was now unwilling to procure even 20-30 per cent of the ethanol produced. 
 Patil also called for an investigation into alleged irregularities in ethanol blending, arguing that the mismatch between production and procurement had created difficulties for the sector.
